overall_reason: The layout is built for other languages (logical properties, [dir=rtl], a language switch), but a scheduling product shows three time formats on one page, downloads its display font twice and needs script for half its text.

score.reason: T-WIDTHS and T-RTL-READY pass; T-LOCALE-FORMAT (ROB-012), T-WEIGHT-FOR-JOB (ROB-018), T-NO-SCRIPT (ROB-015) and T-TRANSLATE on the header (ROB-011) fail.

findings.title: Dates, numbers and money follow one locale
findings.where: Inbox mock, booking slots and hero chip, 375px, tiles/375-03.png and tiles/375-00.png
findings.evidence: formats.mixed_on_one_surface: '12-hour and 24-hour times'. The inbox mock shows '13:40', '11:03' and '09:52'; the booking card below shows '9:30am' and '10:00am'; the hero chip shows '2:00 AM' (tiles/375-00.png). That is three styles: 24-hour, lowercase am and uppercase AM.
findings.before: Each product mock formats time its own way.
findings.after: Format every time on the page from one locale setting (Intl.DateTimeFormat with the visitor's locale), the way the product would.
findings.why: For a scheduling product whose pitch is time zones, mixed formats on the home page suggest the product will mix them too.

findings.title: Weight fits the page's job
findings.evidence: performance.heaviest: https://cal.com/_next/static/media/CalSansVF-s.p.051r2yy2270w-.woff2 (146 KiB) and https://cal.com/_site/_next/static/media/CalSansVF-s.p.1_01gtw8uoq3u.woff2 (144 KiB): the same variable face from two app builds. Fonts total 337 KiB (font_kib fail over 320); 187 requests (fail) and JS 713 KiB (warn).
findings.before: Two Next.js apps on one page each ship their own copy of Cal Sans.
findings.after: Serve one CalSansVF file from one shared URL to both apps.
findings.why: Every visitor downloads 144 KiB twice for one typeface.

findings.title: Content and navigation do not depend on script
findings.evidence: resilience: scripts off shows 3880 of 8901 characters (43.6% of baseline); the sweep's hidden_content hits (ROB-001, Floor) record 52% invisible. console_errors 35, including "Refused to execute script from 'https://cal.com/1100e7f5c1bf1a7d/script.js' because its MIME type ('text/html')", 404s and 429s.
findings.before: Half the page waits for script, and the page throws 35 errors while loading.
findings.after: Render the section text in the server HTML; remove or fix the script path that returns an HTML page.
findings.why: A failed or blocked bundle leaves a marketing page with half its argument missing.

findings.title: Room for other languages
findings.where: Header nav (Products, Use cases, Features, Resources, Enterprise, Pricing), 1280 and 1440px, tiles/1440-00.png
findings.evidence: controls.fixed_width_buttons_tight: 'Products' 104px box, 27% room; 'Use cases' 24%; 'Features' 28%; 'Resources' 23%; all nowrap. rows_without_room_for_35pct at 1280: six items, free_px 58 against needed 129. The footer has a language switch ('English', tiles/1440-15.png).
findings.before: Fixed-width nowrap triggers fill the header row at 1280.
findings.after: Size triggers to their labels and move the nav into the menu when the row has no room.
findings.why: The site offers other languages, and German or French labels 35% longer will not fit the row at 1280.

strengths: Logical properties are used throughout (587, with 279 start and end), and the stylesheet has [dir="rtl"] rules and :lang(ar) rules.
Inbox previews truncate with an ellipsis inside rows that keep the sender and time (tiles/375-03.png).
The hero heading with its inline chips rewraps at 375 (tiles/375-00.png) and the document matches every viewport width.
not_investigated: T-STRESS: no hostile content was injected; long names, translations and missing images are reasoned from layout evidence, not observed
right-to-left render: not captured; readiness read from the stylesheet only
page load on a throttled line: only actions were held slow
layout shift as a number: this capture predates CLS recording
computed text-overflow per element: absent in this capture; ellipsis rows come from class rules and were checked on tiles
widths between the captures, 320px and landscape
regions behind menus, tabs, dialogs or a login that the capture did not open
the failed path: the one held action did not respond at 0.5 or 2 s but made no same-origin request, so there was nothing to fail; CMP-001 is the sweep's
fallback face: 2 font requests were blocked by the capture network (not verified)
the 140 words hidden at 375 are the sweep's phone_parity hit (ROB-002)
contract: no 00-contract.md; inferred a Persuade home page for an international scheduling product with a language switch
